summary: Full e2e testing of the two new features: 'Subida de Canciones' (admin songs CRUD + chunked MP3 upload to Emergent object storage) and 'Letra Sincronizada' (synced lyrics on song page). Backend: 6/6 new pytest in tests/test_songs.py pass (public listing shape, admin auth guard on /api/admin/songs + /api/admin/upload/{chunk,complete}, himnos invalid-group → 422, non-audio extension → 400, /complete mismatched total → 400, and the full chunked-upload → song-create → public-list → audio-stream (size-exact match) → slug-collision → delete → audio-404 lifecycle). Pre-existing suite tests/test_api.py (9/9) still green. Frontend: admin login, default 'Canciones' tab, SongForm fills + chunked upload (song-audio-selected appears), submit creates row in songs-admin-list ('1 registros'), songs-admin-item-link navigates to /canciones/otras/<slug>, public song page renders song-lyrics + 'Audio disponible'. SyncedLyrics: idle status 'Pulse un verso para escuchar'; clicking a verse starts playback and global-player-bar becomes visible; after ~7s a p[data-testid=current-line] exists and a [data-testid^=stanza-][data-active] is set; synced-status flips to 'Sincronización estimada'; synced-follow-toggle flips aria-pressed true→false. Edit flow (songs-admin-edit-{id}) persists title change; delete flow (songs-admin-delete-{id} → confirm) removes from admin list AND from public /api/songs. Libro de Visitas tab still shows moderation-panel; admin-logout works. Regression: home, /canciones/otras/sielvientosopla still work. All created test data was cleaned up (GET /api/songs returns [] at end of run).

integration_issues.flow: Letra sincronizada — seek on later verse
integration_issues.issue: While audio was playing (player-time-current=0:08), clicking the last verse (lines[-1]) with 4 lyric lines caused the time to drop to 0:01 instead of jumping forward (expected ~70% of duration ≈ 1:05 based on buildTimeline). Timeline computation looks correct in SyncedLyrics.jsx line 46-47 (seek(t.start)); likely cause is `live` being transiently false at click time (dur===0 edge case) which makes jump() fall into the `!live` branch and call play(...) from zero. Only reproduces on freshly-created songs — the static sielvientosopla seeks correctly in prior iterations. Low priority as all other sync behaviour (status, current-line, data-active stanza, follow toggle) works.

action_items: Investigate SyncedLyrics.jump(): guard against dur===0 by waiting for metadata before falling back to play()-from-zero, so that a user clicking a later verse immediately after the global player bar appears actually seeks forward instead of restarting.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/songs.py: _audio_cache is an in-process dict with crude 40-entry clear() eviction — fine for the small owner-only archive but note it does not survive restarts and offers no per-key TTL.

routes/songs.py: /admin/upload/chunk accepts any `upload_id` matching [a-f0-9-]{8,64} with no server-side session binding to the authed user. Any admin can resume another admin's upload. Low risk (single-owner site) but worth binding upload_id to user id in Mongo.

routes/songs.py: MAX_AUDIO is enforced via sum of on-disk parts in /tmp/apl_uploads — on a /tmp purge between chunk and complete the request returns 400 'Faltan fragmentos' instead of a cleaner 410/409 'upload expired'.
routes/songs.py: Streaming endpoint returns the entire body with `Accept-Ranges: none` — mobile Safari will refuse to scrub. Consider implementing byte-range support for better UX on long audios.
SyncedLyrics.jsx: buildTimeline estimation relies on Math.max(text.length, 14); very short/empty-line stanzas can shift timing significantly. Documenting as 'estimated' is fine for v1.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (10/11 scripted assertions passed; seek-forward observation flagged)

rca of the issue: SyncedLyrics seek-backward observation — Hypothesis: In SyncedLyrics.jsx the `live` flag is `Boolean(file && track?.file === file && dur > 0)`. Immediately after the first click starts playback via play(...), the audio element metadata (and thus `dur`) may not yet be set when the test clicks the last verse; `live` is therefore false and jump() takes the `!live` branch calling play(...) again — which internally resets currentTime to 0 (hence the 0:01 reading). Mitigation: await loadedmetadata before considering the audio 'live', or in jump() when !live but file matches current track, call seek(estimatedStart) after the metadata-loaded promise instead of restarting. Not reproducible on static songs where dur is cached across visits.
